output.summary: KEP-3000 (Artifact Distribution Policy, owned by sig-release) proposes a policy and procedure to promote Kubernetes container images to multiple registries and mirrors, plus URL redirection to local cloud or country mirrors. Its status is provisional, stage alpha.
output.rationale: The readme cites rising distribution cost (about $150k USD/month, mostly egress) and countries whose firewalls block access to official release images. The proposal extends the image promoter to push to multiple providers, or syncs from production buckets, and adds a redirection layer. The discussion attached to this KEP, however, is about the kubelet node sizing plugin (PR #2370, KEP number 2369), not about artifact distribution, so it does not explain this KEP's design choices.

alternatives.option: Extend the existing image promoter to push directly to multiple providers
alternatives.why_not: Listed in the readme as the first option in the proposal, but the source does not say why it was preferred or rejected.

alternatives.option: Run a second process to synchronize images from existing production buckets to other providers
alternatives.why_not: Offered in the readme as an alternative; the source gives no stated reason for choosing or dropping it.

evidence.quote: The cost of distributing Kubernetes comes at great cost nearing $150kUSD/month (mostly egress) in donations.
Alternatively we use a second process to synchronize container images from our existing production buckets to similar constructs at other providers.
Additionally we require a registry and artifact url-redirection solution to the local cloud provider or country.
the KEP number (in the title of this PR, the `kep.yaml` file, the directory name, the PRR filename, and the title line of the KEP `README.md`) should match the issue number
